project.name: TRACE
project.one_liner: an app that protects elderly and first-time digital banking users from scam calls and coerced payments, traces stolen money in the golden hour, freezes only the tainted amount, and immunises the whole network against the next attempt

requirements.text: Demo user (Lakshmi, 68) can pay a known payee by UPI in the simulated banking app with zero added friction and no intervention

Call screening reads a live or scripted call transcript and flags the five social-engineering script markers (authority claim, threat, isolation instruction, payment demand, verification blocking) with a rising risk indicator

Coercion Score at payment combines: active call, remote-access app present, first-time payee, pasted VPA, app-switching, and hesitation typing dynamics measured on the amount field; breakdown is visible
Graduated response from the score: allow, soft check, hold with co-sign, hard stop with named rebuttal; never a binary block

Voice interview: when held, the app asks the user in plain words who the money is for and why; accepts speech or typed text; classifies against a scam taxonomy; shows the exact scam name, a one-line rebuttal and a sourced statistic
Trusted Circle: a held payment pushes full context to a guardian screen (daughter) with one-tap approve or veto; the customer chose the circle themselves
Retrieval: from a stolen amount, simulate and visualise the money-flow tree across at least four layers with a golden-hour countdown and settlement-point detection

Proportional Freeze: pro-rata (haircut) taint, per-hop dilution and a de-minimis floor; ledger shows held vs free per account; the ₹20 to tea-shop then ₹10 to customer case results in ₹20 held and ₹0 held respectively

Network immunity: a confirmed incident publishes the mule VPA and script signature to a network registry; a later payment attempt to that VPA is blocked before it starts, with the reason shown; a network view lists what is now immune
Every classifier works deterministically offline; an LLM key is optional and only improves wording
Single runtime, starts with one command, in-memory state, one-click demo reset
Presenter panel triggers the five demo beats deterministically and can also drive scenarios live (start call, toggle remote-access app, inject payee)
Verified-link shield: typing a customer-care search intent is intercepted with the verified number and in-app help instead of search results
Evidence pack: a confirmed incident generates a simulated NCRP/CFCFRMS/STR-format report with confidence threshold and a human-confirm step
Caller reputation: a number that ran the script on one user is flagged on the network before the next call
Privacy: all coercion signals compute in the browser; only the score and its category breakdown leave the device
Works at phone width and on a projector; large-text mode; keyboard operable
Synthetic-media (voice/face clone) indicator shown on curated demo samples
Loan-app checkpoint: before a lending app payment, check lender against an RBI regulated-entity list and flag predatory pattern
Guided booking agent that pays within a user-set limit (demo)
Card-fraud ML engine and crypto off-ramp tracing

Caller Attestation: institutions attest a call through the customer's app before it rings; an unattested authority claim on an active call is flagged as fraud by definition, and the phone says so in plain words

Duress PIN: the user registers a second PIN; entering it under pressure shows a true under-verification receipt with a reference and window, holds the funds, alerts the guardian and starts the interview
Scam Rehearsal: a consented drill runs a simulated scam call at the user; the outcome is shown as a gentle lesson and tunes that user's personal intervention thresholds
Un-isolate: during a flagged live call, one tap conferences the guardian into the call; the simulated scammer disconnects when a third party joins
Campaign detection: the same script fingerprint across many users in a short window raises network-wide thresholds and is named on the network view

assumptions.text: User delegated requirement sign-off ('forget me, I want to win'); all must/should requirements treated as agreed; could-haves built only if time remains after the five demo beats work
Bank, NPCI, police and FIU rails are simulated in-process; no real money, no real PIN, no real reporting
Team has Node.js on the demo laptop and Chrome for the Web Speech API; a typed fallback exists for every voice step

decisions.text: One runtime: Next.js app with route handlers, in-memory state, clients poll every 400ms
decisions.rationale: No second service, no database, no websockets: nothing to fail at hour 18. Polling is enough for four screens on one laptop.

decisions.text: Deterministic taxonomy classifier is primary; LLM is an optional enhancer behind an env key
decisions.rationale: Venue wifi is unreliable; the stage demo must never depend on a network round trip
Built backwards from the five demo beats

decisions.text: Five inventions added on user request: caller attestation, duress PIN, un-isolate conference, scam rehearsal, campaign detection
decisions.rationale: Each changes who holds power in the scam; each is cheap on simulated rails. Attestation and duress PIN are must-haves; the other three are should-haves built after the five beats work.

User chose laptop + hotspot hosting. The Next.js server already is the backend; adding Firestore would remove the works-with-wifi-off guarantee. Documented as a one-file swap in DEPLOYMENT.md if internet hosting is ever needed.

decisions.text: Card model trained in Python once, scored in TypeScript at runtime
decisions.rationale: Mirrors Tek-nr/AI-Based-Fraud-Detection (imblearn balancing + XGBClassifier + held-out metrics) on PaySim, but keeps one runtime on stage. Parity test asserts TS matches Python within 1e-4.

risks.text: Scope: the concept has ten capabilities; the 24-hour build ships one spine touching all three pillars
Web Speech API needs Chrome and often needs network; typed fallback is mandatory
Overclaiming freeze or police-reporting authority on stage; every simulated rail is labelled as simulated
PaySim is synthetic: 99.6% recall and ROC-AUC 1.000 are an upper bound, not real-world card-fraud performance

authentication.evidence: No user accounts in the prototype; the two demo PINs are documented constants (README) checked in the reducer. Production would sit inside the bank app's existing authentication.

authorization.evidence: Every mutating request carries x-trace-role; src/app/api/action/route.ts rejects unknown roles with 403 and src/lib/store.ts PERMISSIONS refuses actions outside the role (cosign.decide guardian-only, demo.* presenter-only). Verified by hand with curl and by the role table.

input_validation.evidence: zod schemas on every POST body (action, classify, screen); amount bounded to (0, balance] and payload fields coerced by str()/num() in the reducer; illegal state transitions throw ActionError 409 without mutating state (store.test.ts 'illegal transitions').

secrets.evidence: Only OPENROUTER_API_KEY/OPENROUTER_MODEL, read from process.env in src/lib/llm.ts; .env is git-ignored; .env.example carries no values; the key is never logged or returned to clients.

database_access.evidence: In-memory state only; no database, no query construction.

api_security.evidence: Distinct 400/403/409 responses with plain messages; unexpected errors log server-side and return 'internal error' (no stack traces); GET /api/state is no-store; same-origin fetches only; no CORS opened.

sensitive_data.evidence: Keystroke timings are reduced to one index in the browser (src/lib/hesitation.ts) and only the index is posted; microphone audio is transcribed in the browser and only text is posted; no real PINs, names or accounts (fictional seed).

common_web_vulnerabilities.evidence: No dangerouslySetInnerHTML, eval or dynamic script; React escapes all rendered text; no cookies or sessions to CSRF; the role header is documented as demo-only, not a production boundary.
